status_basis: Workload values decided by the heavy delegate under the owner's standing delegation (workload_decision; not owner-signed). Both levels' maintenance/retention measured and full footprint/workset coverage 9/9 at both levels (level-1 20261111T161111518028Z, level-2 20261111T204640551313Z); local measure_feasibility gate reports no other reason (decisions.footprint_closure_2026-11-11). Local x86_64 classification only; not ARM64/target qualification.

levels_note: two load/cardinality levels (plan 117, spec 393); level-2 is about twice level-1

baseline_min_eligible_windows.source: project implementation plan; project design specification

safety_free_fraction_min.source: project implementation plan; project design specification

ram_budget_ceiling_bytes.source: owner decision (2026-11-11, local-first): reduced 12 GB -> 6 GB for safety; start value, expand later

cpu_budget_ceiling_cores.source: owner decision (2026-11-11, local-first); numeric value carried over from plan:23 / spec:349

reconciliation_range_seconds.source: project design specification (W has no production-safe value); builder proposal

kafka_swap_topic_budget_bytes.formula: ton.swap_events.v1, 1 partition at 2 GiB; envelope requires events_per_second*payload_bytes*86400 <= this

field_definitions.baseline_fanout: prior feature windows read per scored token-window per detector (7d/5min); identical at both levels because the lookback is fixed by policy
field_definitions.zero_grid_rows: explicit zero/missing/inactive rows retained for token-windows with no activity
field_definitions.scan_membership: key+digest manifest rows per reconciliation walk
field_definitions.active_wallets: distinct trader wallets within the 7-day baseline horizon
field_definitions.latency_seconds: objective: action_end to accepted feature/alert row
field_definitions.catchup_seconds: objective: time to drain outage backlog back to steady state
field_definitions.outage_seconds: injected local outage duration absorbed without data loss

local_host_measurement.note: Measured limits of the local x86_64 host only; not ARM64 evidence; not a workload.

constraints: ram_budget_bytes and cpu_budget_cores fixed by owner as local ceilings

target_id.rationale: Project is local-first; the only evidenced execution host is the local x86_64 machine running compose project ton-sentinel-task02-local and k3d cluster ton-sentinel-local (8 CPUs, MemTotal 16025497600 B).
target_id.source: retained local evidence record (uname -m, nproc, /proc/meminfo); retained local evidence

ram_budget_bytes.rationale: owner-fixed local RAM ceiling, reduced from 12 GB to 6 GB for safety (2026-11-11); expand later

events_per_second.unit: accepted swap actions/s (network-wide STON.fi+DeDust, both directions)
events_per_second.rationale: Modest sustained average for the first local level. No source-derived rate exists (live reads not authorized; spec 355: no fixed throughput claim). Bounded so 24 h of broker ingress (eps*payload_bytes*86400) stays within the 2 GiB single-partition ton.swap_events.v1 budget at both levels.
events_per_second.source: project design specification; project implementation plan (Kafka 24-48 h candidate); deploy/helm/ton-sentinel/storage-budget.json; deploy/helm/ton-sentinel/STORAGE.md:15,39-42

payload_bytes.rationale: Synthetic fixture actions are 425-716 B compact JSON but omit real transfer/peer-swap/route/trader evidence (spec 6.1); 2000 B gives ~2.8x headroom over the largest fixture. Level-2 4000 B equals the source client's own per-item ceiling at a full page (4,000,000 B body / 1000 items), modelling heavy multihop payloads.
payload_bytes.source: tests/fixtures/truth/actions.json (synthetic; compact JSON 425-716 B per action); src/ton_sentinel/source/client.py:68-69 (max_body_bytes=4_000_000, max_page_items=1000); project design specification

active_tokens.unit: tokens in the versioned data-derived active-token universe
active_tokens.rationale: Spec 279 materializes the zero grid only for a data-derived active-token universe; all tokens remain in ingestion scope (plan 16). With eps*300 s = 600 actions/window, this many tokens means most token-windows are sparse, the worst case for explicit zero rows.
active_tokens.source: project design specification; project implementation plan

active_wallets.unit: distinct trader wallets within the 7-day baseline horizon
active_wallets.rationale: Assumption, no wallet cardinality in any doc: events in 7 d = 1209600 ; ~12 swaps/wallet/week mean gives ~1e5 distinct wallets. Drives exact unique_traders state for active_wallets_spike.v1.
active_wallets.source: project design specification; project implementation plan

zero_grid_rows.rationale: Worst-case upper bound: every active token has an explicit row for every retained derived window (active_tokens * 8640, 30 d * 288). Real zero rows are fewer.
zero_grid_rows.source: project implementation plan; project design specification; acceptance.json derived.derived_retention_windows_per_token

scan_membership.unit: key+digest manifest rows per reconciliation walk
scan_membership.rationale: eps * W with proposed range width W = 3600 s (derived.reconciliation_range_seconds). Spec 165: no production-safe W yet, so W is a builder proposal for local measurement only.
scan_membership.source: project design specification; project implementation plan

reconciliation_per_hour.unit: reconciliation attempts/hour (each 2 agreeing, max 3 full walks)
reconciliation_per_hour.rationale: One attempt every 900 s (level-1: every 15 min = 3 windows; level-2 doubles the cadence as a stress level). Worst case 4*3 walks*7200 rows = 86400 manifest rows/h. Sweep interval R has no production-safe value (spec 165).
reconciliation_per_hour.source: project implementation plan; project design specification

corrections_per_hour.rationale: 1% of hourly events (eps*3600/100). No correction rate exists in any doc; 1% is a deliberately non-trivial rate so repair/rescore paths (7-day baseline rescoring) are exercised.
corrections_per_hour.source: project design specification (6.3 revision policy); section 288 (corrections rescore following windows); retained local evidence

maintenance_seconds.unit: seconds of serialized PG/retention maintenance per run
maintenance_seconds.rationale: Two 5-min windows at level-1, doubled at level-2 (more rows to vacuum/expire). Must run through the one shared fenced maintenance slot and not overlap replay/peaks; actual duration must be measured.
maintenance_seconds.source: project implementation plan; project design specification

backlog_events.rationale: Recomputed on 2026-11-11 as events_per_second x outage_seconds (level-1 1200, level-2 2400), matching measured backlog 1213 and 2487.

outage_seconds.unit: seconds of injected local downstream/ingest outage
outage_seconds.rationale: Reduced to 600 s on 2026-11-11 (workload decision): shorter outage keeps the run within the 2.5 h budget while still exercising restart and catch-up.
outage_seconds.source: project implementation plan; project design specification

latency_seconds.unit: seconds from action_end to accepted feature/alert row
latency_seconds.rationale: Level-1: one 5-min window plus up to 600 s safety lag/watermark (final append outputs trade latency for correctness). Level-2 relaxed 2x under doubled load. Spec 393 requires numeric SLOs fixed before test; spec 355 forbids presenting them as throughput/latency claims.
latency_seconds.source: project implementation plan; project design specification; retained local evidence

catchup_seconds.unit: seconds to drain the outage backlog back to steady state
catchup_seconds.rationale: Set to 900 s on 2026-11-11 (workload decision), within the 2x outage bound.
catchup_seconds.source: project design specification (catch-up rate and accepted recovery time)

run_seconds.unit: seconds (wall-clock bound of the measured run)
run_seconds.rationale: Set to 9000 s on 2026-11-11 (owner standing delegation): steady 7500 s covers the 7200 s baseline minimum (plan:19); outage 600 s and catch-up 900 s. Supersedes the earlier 5100 s value.

workload_decision.authority_statement: Owner standing rule: owner-level decisions are not sent back to the owner; the heavy delegate decides them autonomously and records rationale. This is NOT an owner signature.
workload_decision.rationale: All load/cardinality values (eps, payload, tokens, wallets, zero grid, scan membership, reconciliation, corrections, fan-out) and the latency/catch-up/outage/maintenance objectives are accepted as proposed: each is bounded by a cited constraint (2 GiB swap-topic 24 h budget, 4 MB/1000-item source page ceiling, spec:279 active universe, plan:18 retention, plan:20 walk bound) and no source-derived alternative exists without live reads. run_seconds is revised to remove the real-time cold-start wait (history is seeded at full retained cardinality). Level-2 remains 2x level-1.

backlog_recomputed_2026-11-11.reason: backlog was set when outage was 1800 s; outage was reduced to 600 s, so backlog is recomputed (level-1 1200, level-2 2400). Measured backlog 1213 and 2487 match.

footprint_closure_2026-11-11.reason: Level-2 run 20261111T182826920753Z missed retention_zero_grid_repair: one window after the seeded grid had no events and was never zero-filled, so every correction read 2015 of 2016 baseline windows. Harness fixed (contiguous zero fill from the grid frontier; coverage now requires baseline_rows_read_min >= baseline_fanout). Level-2 re-measured in run 20261111T204640551313Z: coverage 9/9, baseline min/max 2016, grid contiguous. measure_feasibility --mode local --cpu-budget-cores 2 on level-1 20261111T161111518028Z + level-2 20261111T204640551313Z names no reason other than this status flag.
